rationale: Abstract-only: multiple wheeled mobile robots flocking with connectivity/distance stabilization; abstract states simulations and experiments validate controls; flocking observables plausible.
12 real e-puck robots; verbatim inter- vs intra-group average distance segregation metric measured in real experiments, a physical collective observable.
Four physical iRobot Creates; environment-mediated collective behaviors (splitting, corralling) quantified over 30 robot trials with time series (Table III).
Three Amigobot robots flock in bounded room; heading synchronization index Ja and velocity-magnitude synchronization reported from real experiments (verbatim).
Real foot-bots with mutual avoidance; lane formation, order parameter and throughput measured on real robots matching simulations (verbatim).
10 Alice robots in gallery networks; proportion of robots choosing branches and collective path selection measured over hardware replicates.
Seven ComBots flocking deployment; normalized position and velocity deviation (collective configuration/alignment) reported from hardware experiments (verbatim).
iRobot Create flock trials; mean median distance (MMD) flock metric computed for hardware trials across information variants (verbatim).
Hand-bot self-assembly paper reports accessible-volume gains computed geometrically; no measured physical collective observable from multi-robot hardware experiments (full text checked).
Real-robot collective motion experiments; order metric (alignment) and cohesion measured on real robots (verbatim, Fig. 1e).
Jasmine microrobot swarm experiments; information propagation and communication-street building times vs robot number measured (verbatim quotes).
Three e-puck robots under circular formation law; inter-robot angle deviations converging to 2pi/N measured in hardware (verbatim).
Six iRobot Creates flocking trials; inter-agent distance plots for all robots reported (verbatim). Stored abstract is mismatched but full text matches title.
Two foils driven from a common carriage form one self-propelled device modelling fin-fin interactions; not two independent self-propelled agents (verbatim quote).
7 Rovio robots flocking with informed minority; connectivity metric over time reported for real robots (Figure 6, close quote).
4 prototype robots; escape propagation via local interaction with heading angles and angular velocities of robots measured in experiment (Fig. 9, verbatim).
Own analysis is of evolved controllers in simulation; hardware s-bot tests cited from prior work with only success rate, a task-performance measure (full text checked).
Five-robot swarm with triangular lattice flocking; average side-length deviation (lattice order) measured over time in hardware (verbatim).
Six AMiR robots performing BEECLUST-like aggregation; aggregation time vs robot number and cluster formation measured physically (verbatim).
Three Pioneer robots flocking via vision; number of flocks and speed/heading stabilization analysed from hardware runs (verbatim).
8 real Khepera III robots; group speed, mean inter-robot distance error and perimeter measured during real experiments (verbatim).

Full text is Fine & Shell flocking paper (title metadata mismatched; likely duplicate of iros.2011.6048876): six iRobot Creates, inter-agent distances reported. Author should check metadata/duplicate.
Full text is Hauert et al. Reynolds flocking with up to 10 fixed-wing robots (title metadata mismatched); heading std and inter-robot distance change measured in reality.
Four autonomous robots flocking; flock size index measured across guidance, obstacle and bottleneck experiments (verbatim).
4 LEGO NXT robots; polarization and cohesion metrics (cohesion 30-85 cm) measured in hardware experiments (verbatim).
Up to seven Kobots flocking with heading alignment; heading scatter SD and speed of flock migration measured physically (verbatim).
Real multi-robot collective decision experiments; observed quorum 67.9+-8.5% and consensus dynamics reported (verbatim).
8 real e-pucks; self-organized redistribution of robots between areas (e.g. 6 vs 2 robots) and genotype segregation observed in real experiment, beyond dirt level (full text).
Three wifibots leader-follower flocking; inter-robot distances converging to 600 mm reported from real tests (verbatim).
3 e-puck testbed; formation flocking with inter-robot distance errors measured from overhead camera (Fig. 8, verbatim).
Six Pioneer 3-AT robots under physicomimetics; error between desired and achieved swarm radius and max inter-agent distance measured on real robots (full text).
Four real wifibots in leader-follower flocking; cohesive radius and minimum inter-robot distance reported over experiment (Fig. 3).
Up to 12 physical s-bots self-organize into chains and transport teams; group sizes (Table VII) and sub-task dynamics reported, beyond pure success rates.
iRobot Creates emergent flocking via leader following; team centroid-leader distance and group radius measured over hardware trials (close quotes).
Macroscopic models compared against 15-Jasmine BEECLUST hardware experiments; mean number of aggregated robots per zone from robotic experiments (verbatim).
Four car-like robots in following/flocking modes; measured travelling courses and speeds of robot followers reported; weak but present hardware interaction observable.
Macroscopic self-propelled floating units (not colloids) self-assemble; cluster formation and rotation onset at exactly six units observed in experiments.
Khepera robots with interaction forces; order of formation measured in robot experiments (verbatim formula and trajectories).
Three-vehicle testbed with Morse-potential interactions; experimental leader-following thresholds vs distance reported, comparing with simulations; hardware comparison exists so not E2.
10 e-pucks reach collective wall-following decision via local radio; convergence times vs transmission power measured (verbatim).
Paper includes multi-robot pheromone experiment (4-17 robots) with fundamental diagram flow/velocity vs density (verbatim); not biology-only.
Pioneer II robots flocking experiments with stability times and inter-robot configuration reported (text partly garbled); primary hardware flocking study.
Real robots with virtual field; number of robots in each state over time (proportion regulation) measured in hardware (verbatim, Fig. 8).
Hardware metrics are inspection completion time and redundantly inspected blades (task performance); per-state robot counts come only from the model (full text).
10-20 Alice robots; largest aggregate size, number of aggregates and choice distributions measured in hardware (verbatim).
Two wheeled robots plus virtual leader; velocities, orientations and separations converge (0.113 m/s) in experiments (verbatim); two-body qualifies.
Alice robots aggregation: largest aggregate size, number of aggregates and shelter choice measured in hardware (verbatim).
Six walking robots economic model; reports only ore collected and counts of sales/operations per robot, task outputs without physical collective observable (full text).
Over 20 physical robots, 50+ trials per behavior; real-robot data for following, dispersion, aggregation, flocking with convergence evaluation (verbatim).
Multi-robot V-DEAR experiments; working-state ratio of robots (about 1/3) and trail formation measured (close quotes).
Linked module cluster robot; reports only object enclosing/molding outcomes and times (task performance), no collective observable of the agents (verbatim quotes).
Five car-like robots; group centroid, orientation and shape variables s1, s2 measured in hardware experiments (verbatim).
5-40 hardware robots; communication signal propagation (reception frequency) and gathering patterns measured from robot interactions (verbatim).
Eight robots flocking with on-board localisation; maximal inter-robot distance within flock (5-6 robot lengths) reported (verbatim).
10 real Moorebots; flocking performance vs number of neighbours N significant by ANOVA on real robots (close quote).
Real-robot part (five LinuxBots) reports only trajectory lengths for guiding a robot to a beacon; voting dynamics only in simulation (full text).
Only one Army Ant robot was available; other heartbeats are standalone circuits, so fewer than two physical self-propelled agents (verbatim).
Two free-flying robots capture and dock an object; reports trajectories and force estimates as task/control performance, no collective observable.
Only simulations of 500 bristlebots with parameters extrapolated from prior hardware data; no new hardware experiments or direct hardware comparison (verbatim).
Spring-coupled active Brownian robot dimer studied by theory and simulation only; parameters matched to prior experiment [13], no hardware data here (verbatim, full text).
Experiments use a single programmed bristlebot pushing passive wooden cubes; no second active agent (verbatim, confirmed in full text).
Janus swarmalator model studied by simulation and control theory; no robotic hardware experiments (verbatim quotes).
MagTile platform: two magnet agents' tracking errors, collision-avoidance counts and distances are control/task metrics; no physical collective observable.
Abstract-only doctoral thesis record (DOI thesis prefix) summarising UAV swarm work; no quantitative collective result in abstract; thesis likely compiles published articles.
Abstract-only: chain-flocking navigation validated mainly in simulation, implemented on robots; reports only formation/obstacle-passing task outcomes.
Zenodo dataset record accompanying a submitted RA-L paper, not itself a research article (verbatim).
Bristlebot age-mismatch study is in-silico only; authors state physical pilot experiments await construction (verbatim).
Conceptual framework paper (NLM methodology) describing prototypes without measured results or quantitative data (full text checked).
Swarmalator navigation with vehicle constraints validated only in simulation, as authors state (verbatim).
Two-robot master-slave platform; only obstacle detection success and RF packet-loss engineering metrics, no collective observable (verbatim).
Three TurtleBots in formation; only trajectory tracking RMSE and obstacle avoidance performance reported (verbatim).
Platform built on PX4/Gazebo/ROS2; flocking and stigmergy coverage results are from simulated vehicles, no physical robot data (full text).
Robot hardware narrow-road crossing reported qualitatively; pressure-volume and phase separation are from 1200-robot simulations; ant data biological (full text).
Magnetic soft swimmer collectives studied purely by computational fluid-structure simulations (verbatim).
Phase diagrams/circliness are from simulation; TurboPi robot validation only qualitatively reproduces behaviors, no hardware collective measurement (full text).
Four Crazyflies: real flights show trajectories and repeatability only; alignment and virtual-force metrics computed in simulation (full text).
Five LIMO robots physical demonstration is qualitative; flocking metrics (annulus rate, collisions) from simulation only (full text).
E-puck experiments are run in Webots simulator; no physical robot experiments (verbatim).
Balboa robot formation via distributed optimization; only convergence error/function value reported, task performance.
Abstract-only: CrazyFlie swarm experiments described qualitatively (structure preserved); no quantitative collective observable in available text.
Magnetoactive Janus particles driven by uniform external fields, no programmable or feedback control of agents (verbatim).
Six Bubble robots for inspection; only target tracking error and coverage metrics reported (verbatim).
Authors state all results come from a simulated model of their robot system; no new hardware data (verbatim).
Crazyflie flocking hardware shown only as snapshots/video; quantitative completion rates are from simulation (verbatim, full text).
Centrally commanded light-field positions robots into arrays; reports trajectory/formation errors (task accuracy), not interaction-driven collective observables.
